newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks close up despite election jitters.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks close up despite election jitters.

text.p: Jakarta stocks closed higher on Wednesday with sustained buying interest in blue chips despite election eve jitters and a hoax bomb threat against the Japanese embassy, brokers said.

The Jakarta composite index rose 3.65 points, or 0.55 percent, to 672.50 points. Decliners led advancers by 60 to 55, with 75 issues unchanged. Total turn-over was around 424 billion rupiah, compared with 320 billion rupiah on Tuesday.
Blue chips Astra International, Telkom, Bank Negara Indonesia and Citra Marga Nusaphala were among the gainers, brokers said.
Analysts and brokers said good first quarter results of some companies such as car maker Astra had boosted sentiment in blue chip counters.

Japan's embassy in Jakarta was evacuated on Wednesday morning after an anonymous phone caller threatened to bomb the building but no explosives were found, police and officials said. This also helped calm nerves, brokers said.
They anticipated slow trading on Thursday, when nearly 125 million people are eligible to vote for 425 elected seats in the House of Representatives. Polls open from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. (0100-0700 GMT).
The central bank clearing house will be closed for the day, which brokers said would affect exchange transactions.
Brokers anticipated further bargain-hunting in blue chips but said there was continued concern over possible post-election violence that could affect the market in the coming week.
Automobile conglomerate Astra closed 300 rupiah higher at 6,375 rupiah after it announced a 63-percent increase in net profit in the first quarter against the same period last year.

One analyst said sustained buying interest in telecommunications firm Telkom was boosted by a recent news report that its subsidiary cellular telephone operator Telkomsel was planning to float its shares later this year.
Telkom will announce its first quarter results on Friday, and brokers said this also helped sentiment. Telkom rose 25 rupiah 25 rupiah to 3,900 on a volume of 4.3 million shares.
But another blue chip, cigarette maker Sampoerna, fell 100 rupiah to 9,325 rupiah despite announcing a rise in its first quarter net profit as the increase was below expectations, brokers said.
"Reports that the government will issue regulations to ban people from smoking in public places also put some pressure on cigarette stocks," a broker with local firm said.

Small-capitalised property firm Mas Murni remained the most active stock, with some 41 million shares traded as profit-taking set in after sharp rises recently on speculation of a rights issue and a take-over.
Mas Murni fell 100 rupiah to 950 rupiah.
